subject: Evaluation sprint: traffic breakdown & success metrics
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@nimbusretail.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop, monica_patel
Date: 2026-11-21T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: Evaluation sprint: traffic breakdown & success metrics

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same frame for the 2-week evaluation sprint. High level goals: validate latency and cost at your peak checkout bursts, confirm model quality on your product description generation flow, and verify seamless routing from your US storefront region to dedicated capacity.

Items covered on the call:
- Primary workload: product description generation used in checkout confirmation and catalog enrichment (sync + async).
- Typical requests: short prompts (~20–80 tokens); longer catalog batch jobs up to ~1,600 tokens.
- Concurrency / burst: baseline 12 RPS, peak bursts to 180 RPS for ~30–90s during promotions.
- SLA expectation: p95 latency < 220ms for single-token responses; cost target aligned to < $0.0009/token equivalent for live flows.

Proposed evaluation sprint (two weeks):
1) Day 0–2: traffic ingest & baseline run (we load your sample payloads into our staging endpoint).
2) Day 3–7: peak/burst simulation and latency/cost measurements.
3) Day 8–11: quality checks against your prompt set and guardrail tuning.
4) Day 12–14: rollup readout and recommendation doc + ops runbook.

Immediate asks from your side:
- Please share sample payloads with real-ish length distributions (inline or attachment).
- Confirm which storefront region(s) we should route to (US-west primary?).
- Identify one engineering owner and one product success metric owner.

Ownership (proposed):
- Redwood: aditya_rao — eval lead, load harness, runburst script, produce readout.
- Redwood SE: lauren_bishop — telemetry dashboard & SLOs.
- Nimbus: Tom Ellis — engineering lead (ingest + test harness access).
- Nimbus: Sarah Park — product success metrics & acceptance.

I attached a simple payload template and a draft sprint timeline. If that looks good, we can kick off onboarding tomorrow and provision a dedicated trial slot.

Attachments: [nimbus_sample_payloads.json (application/json)] [sprint-timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0190

From: Sarah Park <sarah@nimbusretail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimbusretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation sprint: traffic breakdown & success metrics

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with how we saw the flows on our side. Quick answers:

- Payloads: attaching a small sample set (real anonymized items) + a token-length histogram we generated from last quarter.
- Regions: US-west primary, with fall-back to US-east.
- Owners: Tom will be the engineering contact (tom.ellis@nimbusretail.com) and I will own success criteria (conversion uplift and latency thresholds).

A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Our 180 RPS bursts are usually concurrent across ~12 frontend instances (i.e., traffic is evenly sharded). Bursts last ~45–75s typically.
- For batch catalog jobs, concurrency is low (1–4 jobs concurrently) but token lengths average 1,200–1,600 tokens.

We attached the sample payloads and a short PDF describing our acceptance metric definitions. Please confirm receipt and proposed kickoff time tomorrow at 10am PT.

Attachments: [nimbus_sample_payloads.json] [nimbus_token_histogram.pdf]

Best,
Sarah Park
Head of Product, Nimbus Retail
sarah@nimbusretail.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@nimbusretail.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop, monica_patel
Date: 2026-11-22T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation sprint: traffic breakdown & success metrics

Received — thanks Sarah. Confirmed attachments and read the histogram. A couple quick follow-ups before we kickoff tomorrow at 10am PT:

1) Test credentials & ingest method — Tom, can you confirm whether we should pull sample payloads from an S3 bucket or you prefer us to POST to a staging endpoint? If S3, please share a short-lived role or presigned URL.

2) Canary routing — we plan an initial canary at 5 RPS to validate telemetry, then ramp to baseline and burst patterns. Is that acceptable?

3) Acceptance metric: we'll track p50/p95/p99, token cost, and prompt-quality pass-rate (as defined by Sarah). We'll produce a lightweight dashboard (Grafana link) and a short acceptance checklist you can sign off.

Owners & tasks (updated):
- aditya_rao: provision trial endpoint, run smoke canary, produce initial dashboard (Due: Day 2).
- lauren_bishop: create telemetry dashboards and set alert thresholds (Due: Day 3).
- monica_patel: run burst script and validate KV/cache behavior for long-sequence jobs (Due: Day 5).
- Tom Ellis: provide ingest mechanism and test credentials (Due: Day 1).
- Sarah Park: confirm acceptance thresholds and test payload sanity (Due: Day 2).

If that looks good I'll send calendar invites and an initial runbook.

Thanks —
Aditya

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference.com>, lauren_bishop
Cc: Sarah Park <sarah@nimbusretail.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimbusretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation sprint: traffic breakdown & success metrics

Quick technical notes before the sprint:

- For long-sequence catalog jobs (1,200–1,600 tokens) we'll run two parallel execution profiles: 1) FP16 with KV caching enabled, 2) 8-bit quantized profile for cost-sensitive runs. We'll compare latency and memory behavior.
- Batching: we'll auto-batch short prompts up to 32 tokens per request (configurable). Please let us know if you run any strict ordering constraints — batching may reorder across very small time windows.
- Cache warms: plan a 90s warm window before peak burst tests. That will give us representative latency numbers for warmed KV cache states.

Tom / Sarah — please confirm whether catalog batch jobs permit time-windowed reordering (i.e., we can batch across 5–15s windows) or whether you need strict FIFO. That will affect throughput tuning.

I'll post the runbook to the Drive link Aditya shared and drop an Ops playbook snippet into the calendar invite.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.inference.com
